segments.chapter: Piano influences: Teddy Wilson, Tatum and Bud Powell
segments.title: Hearing Teddy Wilson and Billie Holiday on a jukebox at a party
segments.summary: At a Sixth and M Street party he hears Wilson, Holiday, Roy Eldridge and Chu Berry on a record, a turning point in his piano style.

segments.chapter: Piano influences: Teddy Wilson, Tatum and Bud Powell
segments.title: The Benny Goodman Trio and eight years modeled on Teddy Wilson
segments.summary: Hearing China Boy on the radio seals his devotion to Teddy Wilson's style, including the left-hand tenths.

segments.chapter: Piano influences: Teddy Wilson, Tatum and Bud Powell
segments.title: Washington pianists Harold Francis and Dick Hopkins
segments.summary: Harold Francis was the most literate local pianist and showed him Wilson's style; Hopkins played like Earl Hines.

segments.chapter: Piano influences: Teddy Wilson, Tatum and Bud Powell
segments.title: Fats Wright shows him how to play tenths
segments.summary: Roanoke pianist Clyde 'Fats' Wright makes him stretch his hand for tenths, illustrating that he learned from everybody.

segments.chapter: Piano influences: Teddy Wilson, Tatum and Bud Powell
segments.title: Meeting Art Tatum through Booker Coleman and his mother
segments.summary: Tatum stays at Mrs. Coleman's house, listens kindly to every pianist, and Malachi spends days and nights playing with him.

segments.chapter: Piano influences: Teddy Wilson, Tatum and Bud Powell
segments.title: Tatum at the whites-only Maryland club on a spinet piano
segments.summary: Malachi sits by the piano at a segregated club where Tatum plays a poor spinet without complaint.

segments.chapter: Piano influences: Teddy Wilson, Tatum and Bud Powell
segments.title: Bud Powell pushes him off the piano at the Crystal Caverns
segments.summary: In 1942 George Treadwell brings a very young Bud Powell, who takes the bench but blames the console piano.

segments.chapter: Piano influences: Teddy Wilson, Tatum and Bud Powell
segments.title: Leo Williams, the tenor player who matched Charlie Parker
segments.summary: Williams, who toured Chicago with Trummy's band, became Parker's close friend and was called his equal.

segments.chapter: Piano influences: Teddy Wilson, Tatum and Bud Powell
segments.title: Trummy's replacements Swindell and Ike Quebec; Clyde Hart's piano lessons
segments.summary: After Chicago and the Yacht Club, Leo Williams and Harry Curtis leave and are replaced; Clyde Hart shows him piano ideas.

segments.chapter: Piano influences: Teddy Wilson, Tatum and Bud Powell
segments.title: Monk and Bud Powell in New York; Jimmy Dorsey closes the club to hear Charlie Parker
segments.summary: Monk befriends him, and at an after-hours jam Jimmy Dorsey has the doors shut to hear Charlie Parker and offers him a union card.

segments.chapter: Piano influences: Teddy Wilson, Tatum and Bud Powell
segments.title: Bud Powell's verdict, 'he's fast all right'
segments.summary: After a fast, scale-based solo for Coleman Hawkins and Lester Young, Powell's remark makes Malachi realize he needs to say something on the piano.

segments.chapter: Piano influences: Teddy Wilson, Tatum and Bud Powell
segments.title: Billy Kyle and the John Kirby band
segments.summary: He praises Kirby's tight classics-based band and Billy Kyle's underrated piano, which he links to Bud Powell's technique.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: First Eckstine rehearsal in New York: the saxophones and trumpets
segments.summary: He and Tommy Potter reach the June 1944 rehearsal of the seventeen-piece band with Parker, Lucky Thompson, Leo Parker, Buddy Anderson and Dizzy Gillespie.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Jerry Valentine's fast arranging, the trombones and the rhythm section
segments.summary: He describes trombonist-arranger Jerry Valentine, the changing trombone section, bassist Tommy Potter and guitarist Carney Wainwright.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: No drummer, and a book of eight arrangements, some rejected by Basie
segments.summary: Max Roach and Shadow Wilson are unavailable, a white drummer fills in, and the band's few charts include rejects from Basie and Dizzy's Night in Tunisia.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: First dance in Wilmington: Dizzy as straw boss and head arrangements
segments.summary: Dizzy runs the band, calling blues choruses for Malachi and riffs for the sections, and Eckstine asks all writers for charts.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Washington dance, segregation in the South, and drummer Charlie Buck quits
segments.summary: With a white drummer unable to go South, Malachi brings in Charlie Buck, who flees back to Washington after meeting Jim Crow at Rocky Mount.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Improvised drummers across the South and the white drummer sent home
segments.summary: From Columbia, South Carolina, to Tampa they use whatever drummer they can find, while the distressed white New Yorker is sent back.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: The one-nighter route to St. Louis and Art Blakey joining
segments.summary: After a run through the South and Southwest, Blakey arrives in St. Louis and Dizzy corrects his shuffle beat and teaches him to catch breaks.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Young Miles Davis sits in for Buddy Anderson
segments.summary: A high-school trumpeter hanging around the dance hall fills in when Anderson falls ill, until Marion Hazle arrives.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: The Plantation Club in St. Louis and the 'fight' that was Max Is Making Wax
segments.summary: The gangster-run white club wants fast Limehouse Blues to cover fights, dislikes the bebop, and bouncers rush in when the band plays Max Is Making Wax.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Swapping with Jeter-Pillars for a Black club across town
segments.summary: The managers trade bands so Eckstine's group plays a Black club with a chorus line for four weeks.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: The FBI hunts Charlie Parker over his draft call; Charlie Rouse is sent for
segments.summary: Parker is rejected at induction, while Tommy Crump is drafted and Malachi recommends Charlie Rouse as replacement.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Charlie Rouse mesmerized by Parker; Gene Ammons takes the chair
segments.summary: Rouse stares at Parker's solos and misses his entrances, so Eckstine replaces him with Gene Ammons.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Cleveland and the band's growing reputation
segments.summary: In Cleveland, Freddie Webster and Howard McGhee sit in as word spreads about the hip young band.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Charlie Parker pawns a roommate's suit and takes two dollars
segments.summary: Two anecdotes show Parker's persuasive logic: the pawned suit and gently reaching into Malachi's pocket.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Finally understanding Parker's chord extensions
segments.summary: After weeks of not grasping why Parker's notes lay outside his chords, it clicks that he plays extensions, changing Malachi's whole musical outlook.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Dizzy Gillespie as teacher; the pianist as 88-string drum
segments.summary: Dizzy has players sing passages and shows Malachi at the piano how comping should be rhythmic and percussive.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Double-time writing, Dizzy's blues for Eckstine, and thinking in two keys
segments.summary: Dizzy shows him double-time rhythms and the flatted-fifth idea of playing in two keys at once, which he still uses.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Learning from Parker by listening: All God's Children Got Rhythm
segments.summary: At a St. Louis rehearsal Parker takes up a tune Malachi plays and tells him to stop calling changes because his playing came from feeling.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Parker playing along with the radio, and the idea of genius
segments.summary: Parker in his hotel room plays with any radio music; Malachi puts him with Toby Walker, Tatum and later Erroll Garner as geniuses.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Sarah Vaughan as one of the guys in the 21-person traveling group
segments.summary: Sarah Vaughan is a thrill to hear nightly and refuses special treatment among seventeen musicians, a valet and management.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Sarah Vaughan snaps at him at Union Station: 'Go on through the door'
segments.summary: After an all-night stay at a Fourteenth Street after-hours spot, Malachi holds the station door for Sarah and is cursed out, later understanding she wants to be one of the guys.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Sarah the tomboy: foot-races, a dressing-room fight with Boonie, and gin
segments.summary: Sarah races and boxes like the men, kicks trumpeter Marion 'Boonie' Hazle in Boston, and becomes his drinking friend.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Gene Ammons joins in Cincinnati; Lucky Thompson the clean-cut straight man
segments.summary: Ammons becomes a spark of the band, while Lucky Thompson is sober, well dressed and serious.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: A wild band of 19-to-29-year-olds
segments.summary: Used to being the youngest, Malachi finds a band of cussing, drinking, pot-smoking young musicians who all loved each other.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Lucky Thompson's hair straightener burns when the hotel water is cut off
segments.summary: In St. Louis Lucky runs across the street in shorts with lye in his hair and ends up with bald patches, mocked by the band.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Lucky Thompson quits and Dexter Gordon comes in; route to Boston
segments.summary: Lucky leaves in Boston because he cannot stand the band's behavior, and Dexter Gordon replaces him.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Playing Vladimir Horowitz's piano at Boston Symphony Hall
segments.summary: At the band's Symphony Hall concert he discovers the piano he is warming up on was Horowitz's that afternoon.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Preparing for the Apollo Theatre, the supreme test
segments.summary: After a week off to rehearse and get uniforms, the band faces the Apollo, which every Black act saw as the real test.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: The Apollo engagement: long solos by Dizzy and Dexter
segments.summary: The hip New York audience loves Sarah and the soloists, who stretch out for many choruses, unlike earlier big bands.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: The theatre circuit and the Deluxe record date
segments.summary: After Baltimore, Washington and Philadelphia theatres, the band records for Deluxe, whose cardboard-like disks he dislikes.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Opus X chosen for recording; Dizzy's solo over the bridge
segments.summary: Eckstine picks Malachi's teenage-era Opus X, and Dizzy adds a soaring solo over the bridge's big chords.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Opus X's debt to Lunceford Special and Parker's added solo
segments.summary: He later realizes the alto interlude copies a Lunceford arrangement, and Parker asks to add a solo that transforms the piece.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Sides cut: Opus X, Blowing the Blues Away and a slow blues
segments.summary: The date features Jerry Valentine's Blowing the Blues Away with Ammons and Gordon, and Sarah's ballad I'll Wait and Pray is planned.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: The band refuses to record unless Sarah Vaughan records her first song
segments.summary: When the label wants to drop Sarah's tune, she cries, the band says nobody records without her, and Eckstine wins the point.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: The four Deluxe sides and the poor disks
segments.summary: He lists the issued titles, praises Billy Eckstine's songwriting and laments the bad pressings.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Charlie Parker leaves; John Jackson takes the first alto chair
segments.summary: Restless Parker quits before he starts causing trouble and recommends his schoolmate John Jackson.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Charlie Parker's unwritten notes: John Jackson blamed for missing parts
segments.summary: Section mates keep telling Jackson he is missing notes until Dizzy sees Parker had been inventing parts not on the page.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Record companies ignore the band's instrumentals; critics who scorned bebop
segments.summary: The band cut only Opus X and Second Balcony Jump as instrumentals; companies thought only Billy sold records and critics later praised what they once panned.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Parker as first alto in the section, never recorded
segments.summary: He played the lead part like a solo, giving the saxes a free, unwritten sound, but he was never recorded in a section.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Dizzy leaves in January 1945; Fats Navarro replaces him
segments.summary: Dizzy goes out on his own, and the 21-year-old, very heavy Fats Navarro comes in on his recommendation.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Rooming on the road with Dizzy, Parker and Sarah; Fats plays just like Dizzy
segments.summary: Players doubled up in hotels, and Dizzy announced the new trumpeter played just like him; Navarro proved an excellent replacement.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: The New Year's Eve 1944 concert flyer with Parker at the bottom
segments.summary: The advertisement hyped Dizzy, Dexter, Sarah and Blakey but listed Charlie Parker last, showing how little he was known.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Trek through the South and Texas; buying pot, change of trains at El Paso
segments.summary: After the Royal and Howard Theatres the band does a long one-nighter run through Texas, where musicians stock up on cheap marijuana.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Taswell Baird arrested at the Juarez border with the bag
segments.summary: Waiting in El Paso, Malachi lingers in shops while his roommate crosses to Juarez and is caught by the Border Patrol, vanishing for months.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Close call with MPs on the train; Eckstine orders the pot thrown out
segments.summary: Two players hide their stash while military police sit nearby, and Eckstine makes everyone throw theirs from the windows.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Police search the whole band at Los Angeles station
segments.summary: Plainclothes officers search everyone, finding nothing, and watch the band for the six weeks in Los Angeles.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: The Plantation Club in Watts with Billie Holiday, Eckstine and Sarah Vaughan
segments.summary: The band plays a large club on the outskirts of Los Angeles on a bill with Billie Holiday, though nobody yet knows Sarah; she earned about $150 a week.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: Making V-Discs at NBC in Hollywood with Lena Horne, Hawkins and Krupa
segments.summary: Every Monday the band records armed-forces disks hosted by actor Bubbles Whitman, on bills with Lena Horne, Coleman Hawkins and Gene Krupa's trio.

segments.chapter: The Billy Eckstine band, 1944-45
segments.title: San Diego, zig-zagging back east, and Sarah Vaughan decides to go solo
segments.summary: After a pleasant California trip the band returns across the country, and Sarah leaves around the start of summer 1945.

segments.chapter: Trio, Eckstine accompanist and Illinois Jacquet, 1945-48
segments.title: Leaving Eckstine in September 1945 to study, and forming a trio
segments.summary: Convinced he must stop and learn more, he leaves despite Eckstine's protest and forms a Nat Cole-style trio with Tommy Potter and Chester Brown.

segments.chapter: Trio, Eckstine accompanist and Illinois Jacquet, 1945-48
segments.title: Sarah asks to sing with his trio; Mr. Dikes refuses her
segments.summary: Looking for a job for the trio with Sarah Vaughan, he is insulted by a Maryland club owner who will not hire her and never works for him again.

segments.chapter: Trio, Eckstine accompanist and Illinois Jacquet, 1945-48
segments.title: The Off-Beat manager who later plays him a Sarah Vaughan record
segments.summary: Another club owner turns Sarah down, then two years later proudly plays her record, which Malachi takes as proof that owners know nothing about talent.

segments.chapter: Trio, Eckstine accompanist and Illinois Jacquet, 1945-48
segments.title: The trio's success and his short singing career with Route 66
segments.summary: The trio works well around Washington, but his attempt to sing Nat Cole's Route 66 ends when he runs out of breath, and he never sings again.

segments.chapter: Trio, Eckstine accompanist and Illinois Jacquet, 1945-48
segments.title: Eckstine gives up the big band and offers him $100 a week
segments.summary: With the war over and debts of about $25,000, Eckstine goes solo and asks Malachi to be his pianist and musical director.

segments.chapter: Trio, Eckstine accompanist and Illinois Jacquet, 1945-48
segments.title: Last days of 52nd Street: the Onyx Club, road dates and George Shearing's debut
segments.summary: He works the Onyx, tours Baltimore to Cleveland, plays the Royal Roost and a concert where he first hears George Shearing.

segments.chapter: Trio, Eckstine accompanist and Illinois Jacquet, 1945-48
segments.title: The airplane ticket that never came: quitting Eckstine
segments.summary: Starving on $100 a week, he is left without a ticket to the Chicago engagement and decides he cannot gamble further.

segments.chapter: Trio, Eckstine accompanist and Illinois Jacquet, 1945-48
segments.title: Bobby Tucker takes the job; the pros and cons of accompanying
segments.summary: Tucker, who envied his steady job, has been with Eckstine ever since, while Malachi says accompanists rarely get to play.

segments.chapter: Trio, Eckstine accompanist and Illinois Jacquet, 1945-48
segments.title: Eckstine as an artist, and why he had to leave for his family
segments.summary: He credits Eckstine and Sarah Vaughan as literate singers, notes Billy's solfeggio, and says he left only to feed his wife and two children.

segments.chapter: Trio, Eckstine accompanist and Illinois Jacquet, 1945-48
segments.title: Illinois Jacquet's rhythm section and joining his octet at the Apollo
segments.summary: He had furnished Jacquet a rhythm section earlier, and in January 1948 replaces Sir Charles Thompson in the Jacquet group.

segments.chapter: Trio, Eckstine accompanist and Illinois Jacquet, 1945-48
segments.title: Sir Charles Thompson and the dispute over Robbins' Nest
segments.summary: Thompson left after getting no credit or royalties on the hit tune, which opened the job for Malachi.

segments.chapter: Trio, Eckstine accompanist and Illinois Jacquet, 1945-48
segments.title: Shadow Wilson, the hard-swinging drummer
segments.summary: Wilson's concentrated, driving drumming makes everyone in the band play better.

segments.chapter: Trio, Eckstine accompanist and Illinois Jacquet, 1945-48
segments.title: J.J. Johnson's trombone concept in the Jacquet band
segments.summary: Johnson plays fast, articulate lines with a short slide, drawing questions from symphony players.

segments.chapter: Trio, Eckstine accompanist and Illinois Jacquet, 1945-48
segments.title: The Benny Carter school of musicianship
segments.summary: Players who worked for Benny Carter, such as Dizzy, Max Roach and J.J., learned proper section playing and intonation.

segments.chapter: Trio, Eckstine accompanist and Illinois Jacquet, 1945-48
segments.title: Jo Jones replaces Shadow Wilson
segments.summary: Basie's drummer joins the Jacquet band and his experience and stories make working with him a lesson.

segments.chapter: Trio, Eckstine accompanist and Illinois Jacquet, 1945-48
segments.title: Quitting Jacquet over money in September 1948
segments.summary: A pay controversy with Jacquet, partly his own headstrong youth, makes him leave and return to Washington.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: Part 3 opens (7 May 1983); Al Dunn's quartet, Billie Holiday and Dinah Washington
segments.summary: Back in Washington he plays a supper club with Al Dunn's quartet, accompanies Billie Holiday there, then joins Dinah Washington and is typed as an accompanist.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: The 2011 Room house band with Frank Wess, violin and bassoon
segments.summary: In 1950 his sextet is house band in a Black hotel room where Nat Cole and George Shearing's first quintet play, using violin, flute and bassoon in the arrangements.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: Pearl Bailey fills in for Billie Holiday at the 2011 Room
segments.summary: When Holiday cancels, the manager gets Pearl Bailey, who is then asked to go to California.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: Playing the Macombo with Pearl Bailey and losing his band's job
segments.summary: He goes to Hollywood as Pearl's accompanist on promise of better pay, but returns to find his replacement had taken over the club.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: Slow years, then Pee Wee Moore gets him a trial with Louis Jordan's big band
segments.summary: After a drifting 1950-51, baritone player Pee Wee Moore tells him Jordan's new 14-piece band needs a pianist, and he plays one night on trial.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: 'The job is yours. We leave at 9': scrambling to join Jordan
segments.summary: With his wife in hospital and two children at home, he gets Jordan's Monday call and has to arrange childcare and race across town.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: Left behind by the bus, catching up by Trailways, and Jordan's $150 advance
segments.summary: He and the band's one white trombonist miss the departure, reach the dance late, and Jordan gives him money anyway.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: Jordan disbands the big band; re-recording his hits and The Milton Berle Show
segments.summary: Told Jordan netted only five cents on the dollar, the band records 18 to 20 sides and appears on TV before breaking up in December.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: Chris Columbo on a motorcycle seat and 18-year-old arranger Oliver Nelson
segments.summary: He recalls drummer Chris Columbo's showmanship, the teenager who wrote the whole book, and trumpeter Money Johnson.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: A show-business band after Eckstine: shuffle rhythm and chartreuse uniforms
segments.summary: Jordan's music was mostly vocals and shows, a contrast to the Eckstine band, but he finds it enjoyable with good musicians.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: Back with Illinois Jacquet, and bringing in drummer Dude Brown
segments.summary: Jacquet's band is stuck for a drummer in Providence, and Malachi recommends his boyhood friend George 'Dude' Brown.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: George Treadwell offers him Sarah Vaughan's piano chair, with Jimmy Jones ill
segments.summary: Treadwell says Jones will die of lung cancer, but Jones recovers; Malachi stays with Sarah almost two years.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: First dates with Sarah Vaughan in Baltimore and Chicago's Blue Note
segments.summary: They resume as hang-out friends, playing Baltimore and a Chicago club that adores her.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: Bassist Israel Crosby, the legend he most enjoyed working with
segments.summary: A quiet, unassuming bass legend who had played with Fletcher Henderson, Crosby joins Sarah's first trio.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: Drummer Bruz Freeman and the Freeman family
segments.summary: Sarah's drummer is the oldest of the musical Freeman brothers, completing a trio that lasted until Christmas 1953.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: The overloaded excursion boat in Washington with Sarah and Dinah Washington
segments.summary: Too many tickets were sold, people crowd on, the boat sinks lower and the musicians jump to the dock.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: The Biggest Show of 1952 with Nat Cole, Stan Kenton and Sarah Vaughan
segments.summary: Touring with Cole's trio and Kenton's five-section band, he meets Kenton sidemen like Stan Levey and Conte Candoli.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: Paramount Theatre with Jacquet's big band, then sailing to Europe without the trio
segments.summary: After Christmas at the Paramount, Sarah, her husband, valet and Malachi sail on the Liberte because the budget cannot carry Crosby and Freeman.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: London welcome and a BBC broadcast that starts when the BBC wants
segments.summary: Greeted like royalty, they arrive early for the 8 o'clock broadcast and learn British radio starts when it pleases.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: Rehearsing with a Melody Maker-winning British band and touring England
segments.summary: The poll-winning band is eager but young and underprepared in the postwar period, and they tour many English towns.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: Wales, Scotland and Glasgow pianist John Scott Henderson
segments.summary: A Glasgow pianist who knew of Malachi writes ahead and meets him at the station, showing him the town.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: Unheated buses and hotels; Royal Albert Hall
segments.summary: January in Britain with no bus heat and sixpence-meter heaters, which he believes helped bring on arthritis, ends with a packed Royal Albert Hall concert.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: Crossing the Channel to Paris
segments.summary: The train boards the ferry at Dover, and in Paris the problem is the language rather than the money.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: Playing behind the curtain in a swank Paris club
segments.summary: Sarah is the only visible performer while the band led by a Martinique-born flautist plays behind the curtain, making cues a challenge.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: Jazz at the Philharmonic, Sugar Ray Robinson's club and the Chez Sassy
segments.summary: After work musicians gather at Sugar Ray Robinson's club, and a Paris club is named after Sarah.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: Sarah's new trio with Roy Haynes and Joe Benjamin
segments.summary: With Crosby and Freeman gone, Haynes (a frustrated singer who knows every lyric) and Duke Ellington-associated bassist Joe Benjamin join; Haynes is his favorite accompanist drummer.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: Touring the West with Sarah; Storyville in Boston
segments.summary: The trio plays the Blue Note, California, Kansas City and Omaha, then the Apollo, Baltimore, the Howard and George Wein's Storyville.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: After-hours party near Boston; Joe Benjamin's drowsy drinking and earlier car wreck
segments.summary: A club owner hosts the group, and Malachi recalls Joe Benjamin falling asleep after drinking and crashing his Cadillac near a truck.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: The Boston highway crash that left dancer Daisy paralyzed
segments.summary: Sarah rides back with Malachi instead of Joe; moments after Joe speeds past, they find his Cadillac overturned and the chorus girl's spine broken.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: Beverly Peer fills in; Joe's later crashes and death
segments.summary: Beverly Peer substitutes while Joe heals, Joe keeps driving recklessly, and he eventually dies in a car crash.

segments.chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
segments.title: Jimmy Jones returns and he is out of work again
segments.summary: When Sarah takes a summer 1954 vacation Jimmy Jones recovers and resumes his chair, so Malachi returns to Washington and organizes his own jobs.

segments.chapter: Al Hibbler, Dakota Staton and later years
segments.title: Joining Al Hibbler, whose Unchained Melody and He make the best money
segments.summary: Hibbler calls him in late 1954; hits like Unchained Melody and He in 1955-56 bring his highest salaries.

segments.chapter: Al Hibbler, Dakota Staton and later years
segments.title: Hibbler years of shows, Ed Sullivan, Canada and the 1957 British tour
segments.summary: For five years they play all over America and tour London, Liverpool and Glasgow for five or six weeks in 1957.

segments.chapter: Al Hibbler, Dakota Staton and later years
segments.title: Fun with Al Hibbler: train tricks and morning drinks
segments.summary: The blind, jolly Hibbler fakes shivering to board trains early, and they open each morning with scotch and gin.

segments.chapter: Al Hibbler, Dakota Staton and later years
segments.title: Hibbler's popularity wanes; Australia tour with Hawkins, Wilson and Sarah
segments.summary: Around 1960 bookings thin out, but they join a huge Australian tour in stadiums.

segments.chapter: Al Hibbler, Dakota Staton and later years
segments.title: Dakota Staton at the 1960 Newport and Atlantic City festivals
segments.summary: Newport draws a rowdy non-jazz crowd, and in Atlantic City he hangs out with Oscar Peterson.

segments.chapter: Al Hibbler, Dakota Staton and later years
segments.title: Dakota's husband conducting from behind the curtain; he gives notice
segments.summary: Her husband, a former Dizzy trumpeter, micromanages from backstage, and Malachi quits after the Chicago Roberts Show Lounge engagement.

segments.chapter: Al Hibbler, Dakota Staton and later years
segments.title: The late, drunk driver of Dakota's station wagon
segments.summary: After twelve hours' wait the chauffeur shows up, begins swerving, and Malachi takes the wheel for the drive east.

segments.chapter: Al Hibbler, Dakota Staton and later years
segments.title: A hot-rod crash on the rainy Pennsylvania Turnpike
segments.summary: A speeding car with 'Wendy' on the back skids across the median and hits a Mercedes, its engine rolling into Malachi's car.

segments.chapter: Al Hibbler, Dakota Staton and later years
segments.title: At the scene of the fatal wreck, and the end of the Dakota job
segments.summary: He finds three adults dead and two girls injured, the driver barely hurt, and never goes back to Dakota Staton.

segments.chapter: Al Hibbler, Dakota Staton and later years
segments.title: Witness in the Pennsylvania trial: lawyers friendly in the judge's chambers
segments.summary: Called to testify for two years, he is surprised that the prosecutor, defense lawyer and judge chat like old friends.

segments.chapter: Al Hibbler, Dakota Staton and later years
segments.title: Testifying, the girls' letter, and an unknown verdict
segments.summary: The defense lawyer cuts off his answers, he leaves before the jury returns, and he suspects the local boy walked away free.

segments.chapter: Al Hibbler, Dakota Staton and later years
segments.title: Gloria Lynne walks off stage at Basin Street West and fires him
segments.summary: In California her erratic behavior leads the club owner (Wilt Chamberlain) to intervene, and she fires him and refuses to pay his way home.

segments.chapter: Al Hibbler, Dakota Staton and later years
segments.title: Los Angeles Local 47 backs him; a paid vacation and the Ali-Liston fight
segments.summary: The union tells him to keep showing up so he gets his pay and plane fare, and he spends three weeks with Kenny, Nancy Wilson's husband.

segments.chapter: Al Hibbler, Dakota Staton and later years
segments.title: Charlie Byrd's club, Joe Williams and Chicago, then Washington after 1965
segments.summary: He plays two years in Pete Lambros's club with Byrd, tours with Joe Williams, then stays around Washington.

segments.chapter: Al Hibbler, Dakota Staton and later years
segments.title: Bill Harris's Pig Foot workshop and young talents
segments.summary: As musical director he runs a workshop whose young musicians include George Johnson, tied to Eddie Jefferson and James Moody, and singer Rod Willoughby.

segments.chapter: Al Hibbler, Dakota Staton and later years
segments.title: Thanks to Bryant DuPre and closing of the 5 May 1983 session
segments.summary: He credits the young historian with prompting the interview, notes life never goes in a straight line, and proposes a question-and-answer period.

segments.chapter: Addendum on the Eckstine band arrangers
segments.title: 8 May 1983 session opens: more on the Eckstine band
segments.summary: The interviewer records the date, and Malachi says he wants to add people he under-covered in the Eckstine band.

segments.chapter: Addendum on the Eckstine band arrangers
segments.title: Eckstine arrangers: Valentine, Chippie Alcott, Tadd Dameron and Budd Johnson
segments.summary: He describes the band's writers, with Dameron contributing I Want to Talk About You, Our Delight, Air Mail Special and Good Bait, and Budd Johnson also arranging.
